title: Scheduler: TP-group health model (states, quarantine, reset semantics) + rollout gates
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Goal
Implement a TP-group health model in the runtime scheduler so we can:
- stop scheduling new work onto “stuck” or “unhealthy” TP groups,
- quarantine and safely drain/tear down impacted groups,
- reset groups in a controlled way, and
- expose clear metrics + logs so SRE/oncall can distinguish “slow” vs “stuck”.

This is the scheduler-side backbone for the overall TP hang mitigation plan. It should work whether the underlying root cause is (a) collective stalls (NCCL async errors not surfacing), (b) kernel stalls, or (c) scheduler/barrier deadlocks.

Context / problem
We currently treat TP groups as a mostly stateless pool. Under sustained load, groups can enter a no-forward-progress state while still appearing “alive” to the scheduler. The scheduler will continue assigning work, amplifying the blast radius and increasing customer-visible timeouts/5xx.

We need an explicit health state machine and a gating policy to:
- fail fast on the group (quarantine) instead of silently stalling,
- avoid “poisoning” unrelated requests by routing them to the stuck group,
- provide a consistent behavior across Hosted + Dedicated.

Proposed model (high-level)
Introduce a TPGroupHealth state machine owned by the scheduler:

States
- HEALTHY: normal scheduling.
- SUSPECT: forward progress is degraded (soft signal); continue scheduling with caution (optional), or reduce load.
- QUARANTINED: do not schedule new work. In-flight work is either allowed to drain with a short deadline or force-canceled.
- RESETTING: group is being torn down and reinitialized (explicit lifecycle step; scheduler treats as unavailable).
- UNAVAILABLE: cannot be used (e.g., repeated failures); requires operator action or external pool manager to replace.

State transitions (signals)
- HEALTHY -> SUSPECT:
  - watchdog warns on low progress but below “hard stuck” threshold
  - elevated collective latency percentile sustained for X seconds (from metrics in ENG-2404)
  - repeated request-level timeouts concentrated on a single group

- SUSPECT -> QUARANTINED:
  - watchdog hard trigger (no progress for hard threshold)
  - async collective error surfaced (from ENG-2406 / ADR-0147)
  - barrier/cancel invariant violated (from ENG-2403 fix paths)

- QUARANTINED -> RESETTING:
  - group has no in-flight requests OR drain deadline exceeded
  - scheduler has recorded and emitted quarantine reason and counters

- RESETTING -> HEALTHY:
  - reinit completes and basic “heartbeat/progress” check passes

- QUARANTINED/RESETTING -> UNAVAILABLE:
  - exceeds max reset attempts per time window
  - repeated quarantines within window (to prevent thrash)

Scheduler policy / semantics
- Scheduling gate:
  - Only HEALTHY groups are eligible for new placements.
  - SUSPECT groups may be eligible only when pool pressure is high (feature flag), but default is to deprioritize them.
  - QUARANTINED/RESETTING/UNAVAILABLE are never eligible.

- Request lifecycle interaction:
  - If a request is assigned to a group that becomes QUARANTINED mid-flight, scheduler marks request as failed with a distinct error code (e.g., TP_GROUP_QUARANTINED) unless it completes within the drain grace period.
  - Ensure cancellation does not block group reset (ties into ENG-2403).

- Draining behavior:
  - Configurable drain_grace_ms (deployment-mode default).
  - After drain_grace_ms, force-cancel remaining in-flight and proceed to RESETTING.

- Reset semantics:
  - Reset is per TP group, not whole host, to keep failure domain tight.
  - Reset attempts are rate-limited per group to avoid runaway churn during systemic issues.
  - Reset should increment counters and emit structured log with reason + thresholds.

Instrumentation requirements (owned here, implemented with ENG-2404)
- Counters:
  - tp_group_quarantine_total{reason}
  - tp_group_reset_total{reason}
  - tp_group_unavailable_total{reason}
  - tp_group_state_transitions_total{from,to,reason}
- Gauges:
  - tp_groups_in_state{state}
  - tp_group_inflight_requests{group_id}
- Logs:
  - one structured event on quarantine and on reset completion (include group_id, node_id, tp_world_size, model, region, reason, thresholds, last_progress_timestamp)

Acceptance criteria
Functional
1) Scheduler never assigns new requests to QUARANTINED/RESETTING/UNAVAILABLE groups.
2) Quarantine is triggered when watchdog hard threshold fires (ENG-2407) OR when a collective async error is reported (ENG-2406), with a recorded reason.
3) Quarantined groups drain for drain_grace_ms and then reset deterministically; reset path must not deadlock under active cancellations.
4) Rate-limited resets: repeated quarantine cannot create infinite reset loops; after max_resets_per_window, group transitions to UNAVAILABLE.
5) Distinct customer-facing/internal error classification is surfaced at the request layer when group quarantine interrupts a request (so we can attribute timeouts vs forced-fail).

Observability
6) Metrics listed above are emitted and show up in staging; can be used to build alerting/dashboards.
7) Logs contain enough context to debug whether stall is comm vs kernel vs scheduler starvation (exact attribution may be separate, but this ticket must provide the plumbing for reason codes).

Performance
8) No measurable throughput regression >1% on standard perf suite (see ENG-2409) when health model is enabled but no quarantines occur.
9) No additional global synchronization; state checks should be O(1) in scheduling hot path.

Rollout plan (this ticket)
- Feature flag: runtime.tp_group_health_model.enabled (default OFF until canary).
- Canary steps:
  1) Enable in staging + nightly perf-canary TP stress suite (ENG-2405).
  2) Enable in one Hosted high-load pool (us-east, 5% traffic) with aggressive logging and conservative thresholds.
  3) Expand to 25% Hosted once quarantine/reset rates and request error rate are within expected bounds.
  4) Dedicated: opt-in only (per account/cluster flag) with explicit rollback instructions.
- Rollback trigger guidance:
  - sudden spike in tp_group_reset_total without corresponding reduction in timeouts
  - increased 5xx caused by false-positive quarantines (needs reason attribution)
  - any signs of reset deadlock (RESETTING state stuck > reset_timeout)

Implementation notes
- Store TP group health in scheduler’s TPGroup object and enforce eligibility in placement logic.
- Quarantine reason codes should be enumerated (WATCHDOG_NO_PROGRESS, NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR, BARRIER_DEADLOCK_GUARD, RESET_THRASH_PROTECTION, UNKNOWN).
- Ensure scheduler state transitions are atomic; avoid races between watchdog thread and placement thread.

Links
- Design overview: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/tp-stability-hangs-root-causes-and-fix-plan.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0147-tp-collective-timeouts-and-async-error-propagation.json
- Initiative: ENG-2401
- PR (WIP): sources/github/redwood/pr-18432.json (TP-group state machine + scheduling gate)

Open questions
- Do we allow SUSPECT groups to receive new work when capacity is constrained (deprioritize vs hard exclude)? Proposed: deprioritize behind a flag; default OFF.
- Reset ownership boundary: scheduler triggers reset, but actual teardown happens in runtime worker pool; define retry semantics and timeout.

Out of scope
- Implementing watchdog itself (ENG-2407)
- Collective async error propagation details (ENG-2406)
- Dashboard implementation (ENG-2408), but we must provide the metrics/logs.
comments: 2025-02-18 — Sofia Ivanova: Marking P0; this is required to prevent stuck groups from continuing to receive work. Marcus, please prioritize gating logic first (quarantine -> no placement), then add drain/reset semantics.

2025-02-20 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please ensure we have a hard cap on reset loops; we’ve seen thrash during incidents. Also need clear reason codes so oncall can distinguish watchdog false positives vs real comm failures.
2025-02-23 — Marcus Reed: Drafted state enum + placement eligibility check. Remaining: reset rate-limiter + drain grace. Will coordinate with Omar/Julian on metrics naming (ENG-2404).

2025-02-27 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): For rollout, Dedicated must stay opt-in until we have 1 week of Hosted canary data. Add explicit rollback triggers to description (spike in resets; RESETTING stuck).

2025-03-03 — Marcus Reed: Opened PR-18432. Added tp_groups_in_state gauge and quarantine/reset counters. Need review on concurrency (watchdog thread vs scheduler loop) + confirm we’re not adding locks in hot path.

2025-03-04 — Sofia Ivanova: Review feedback—make QUARANTINED a hard gate (no placements) and add UNAVAILABLE state for thrash-protection. Please also ensure request failures surface as distinct internal code (for attribution).
